summary: Add PostgreSQL to an Effect API or React Router app: Compose databases, explicit migrations, a pooled client and per-file test databases.
description: Add local Postgres development and test services to the Effect stacks, with migrations applied by an explicit command and a pooled SQL client owned by the app's layer. A repository decodes every row with Schema and maps constraint errors to tagged errors. The test harness clones a migrated template so each test file gets a private database. Readiness checks the database while liveness stays independent. Product tables, queries and access rules are your work, and production hosting is separate.
seoDescription: Postgres for Effect TypeScript projects, with Docker Compose, Effect SQL migrations, a schema-decoding repository and isolated test databases.

projectExamples.title: Inventory API on Postgres
projectExamples.description: An equipment inventory API that saves records in Postgres, checks incoming data and returns consistent errors when a name is already in use.

projectExamples.title: Booking app with saved reservations
projectExamples.description: A booking app where visitors submit reservations through a web form and see them saved in Postgres for later viewing.

plain.whatItIs: Adds PostgreSQL databases to apps built with Effect, a TypeScript toolkit, with local test databases and saved steps for table changes.
goodAt: Running a local database for development and for tests
Checking database rows against the data shapes the application expects
Making table changes through saved steps that run only when you ask
notGoodAt: Hosting a live production database; arrange a hosting provider separately.
Projects that want query code generated from models; you write the queries yourself.

requests: add a postgres database to my effect api
persist data in postgresql from react router loaders and actions
run sql migrations with an explicit command, not on startup
give each test file its own real postgres database
readiness endpoint that checks the database is reachable
